title: Thirdwatch quick stitch — micro procedures and triage notes
content:
Purpose: quick, compact reference for Thirdwatch (0300–0700) shifts — intentionally terse, meant for rapid handover and fast triage. Treat this file as a living scratchpad.

High-level goals (how I run the shift):
- Watch telemetry dashboards for latency spikes (p50/p95) and queue depth anomalies.
- Keep error budget alerts under 5% of pager noise; escalate only if customers impacted or sustained degradation >10 min.
- Prioritize preserving KV cache and routing fallbacks before routing full model swaps.

Signals to check first (order of ops):
1) Redwood Console "Per-route latency" -> p95 jump on /v1/generate?model=redwood-llama -> check model router and GPU pool.
2) Autoscale events in /dedicated -> any recent scale-in at 02:xx? Might cause cold caches.
3) Redis/KV cache miss rate -> if misses >30% vs baseline, expect slow downstream token generation.
4) Errors surfaced in /streams (streaming aborts) -> look at grpc-proxy logs.

Quick triage checklist (one-liners):
- Confirm alert: slack #sre-alerts screenshot + timestamp.
- ping on-call owner for previous shift (if available): @evan or @priya.
- Check recent deploys: git log --since="4h" infra; look for PRs merged to runtime or router.
- Check model routing rules: curl -s https://console.internal/api/routing?env=prod | jq .routes | grep redwood-llama.
- If latency-only and CPU-bound: consider temporary circuit to a quantized variant (note: quality risk).

Commands / paths I actually use (copy/paste friendly):
- kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/router --since=15m | grep "route=redwood-llama"
- kubectl -n serving exec -it deploy/model-pool -- redis-cli INFO | grep used_memory
- prowctl list jobs --recent --limit 20 | grep deploy | tail -n 10

Temporary mitigations (fast, reversible):
- Route small percent of traffic to fallback region (policy: route.fallback=region-eu) via router config -> helps buy time while investigating degraded pool.
- Turn on prefix caching for frequent short prompts: config key caching.prefix.enabled = true (impact: memory).
- If kv-cache saturated, rotate to secondary shard: redis-cluster scale add-node -> follow infra runbook (linked).

Escalation matrix (who to page if not resolvable in 12 minutes):
- Level 1: current on-call (you) + previous shift contacts.
- Level 2: SRE lead (Priya Rao) + Serving Runtime owner (Siddharth Kapoor).
- Level 3: Engineering manager on duty + Product on-call if customer-facing degrade.
Slack shortcuts: #sre-alerts, #serving-runtime, #oncall-rotations. Use callout template: 
> [TIMESTAMP] Short desc / impact / actions taken / ask (who to help) / rollback plan

Known flaky areas (notes to self):
- Redis cluster node 03 tends to flake after long GC cycles around 02:40 — monitoring shows memory creep after large batch evals.
- Router can mis-route when a canary has incomplete model metadata; check metadata-service logs for 400s.
- Quantized model variant quality drop seen in last-week A/B tests for long-form prompts >1000 tokens.

Handover checklist for next shift (write down actions you started):
- Reordered redis shards and restarted node-05 at 03:22 (observed back to normal by 03:35). Watch mem_used % for 4h.
- Left a canary pinned to region-us-west for redwood-llama-1.1 until 06:00.
- Temporary routing rule: 10% -> fallback-region (ID: cfg/2025-01-09-03) set by me; recommend rolling back if stable at +20m.

Open questions / TODOs (not blocking immediate ops):
- Is there a long-term plan to split KV caches by prompt-class? File a ticket to Product: PRO-993 to discuss.
- Need a short test harness that simulates mixed small/long prompt distributions — spawn a ticket for perf infra.

Short personal notes (quick and messy):
- Coffee low at 03:45, restock in kitchen.
- If you see repeated 503s with empty body -> probably nginx timeout on streaming connection; try increasing streaming.keepalive to 45s and monitor.

Minimal postmortem stub (if incident escalates):
- Incident name: thirdwatch-realtime-latency-YYYYMMDD
- Severity: P1/P2 (choose)
- Timeline: 03:10 alert -> 03:14 triage -> 03:22 mitigation -> 03:34 rollback/partial fix -> 03:50 customer impact ends.
- Owners: triage owner (you), mitigation owner (serving-runtime), communications (customer-success).

References / shortcuts:
- Confluence incident templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Incident+Template
- Perf dashboards: Console -> Observability -> Per-route latency (bookmark saved under "thirdwatch").
- Recent infra PR that touched router: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/312

Final: this doc is intentionally terse. Expand any line above into a full runbook if you find yourself repeating the same mitigations more than twice in a month. Leave comments in the file (add a new bullet with your initials) so we can iterate the compact checklist.

— A.M.
